signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Shock
signals.text: AUD/JPY trades at 109.52 amid severe broad-based divergent currency momentum. On the 1W G10 Strength Scorecard, JPY leads all peers with an average gain of +1.067% across 7 pairs, while AUD sits as the primary laggard averaging -0.807% across 4 pairs, creating an extreme 1.875% bilateral spread. Middle East escalation following reported projectile strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz has sent WTI crude up +2.84% to $93.00, triggering rapid flight into defensive positioning. This flow aggressively challenges the massive +335bp carry advantage of RBA 4.60% over BoJ 1.25% (OIS AONIA 4.60% vs TONA 1.23% at +337bp). COT positioning highlights asymmetric vulnerability as AUD Leveraged Funds hold net long +55,684 contracts while options skew shows heavy downside hedging with EUR/JPY 25d RR at -2.53. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/JPY, high geopolitical risk premium overriding carry support. Catalyst: Tokyo CPI release at 23:30 UTC. Risk: Strait of Hormuz shipping disruptions de-escalate, allowing the +335bp carry buffer to reassert control.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning + Volatility + Fiscal Strain
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1246, breaking down decisively below its SMA20 (1.1501), SMA50 (1.1535), and SMA200 (1.1618) clusters. The macro rate spread remains firmly prohibitive with Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% maintaining a +135bp carry advantage favoring the dollar (OIS SOFR vs €STR at +144bp). Institutional research from ING and Saxo highlights escalating fiscal risks centered on French budget stress, compounding broader European underperformance. FX options markets show elevated demand for downside protection, with 1M ATM implied volatility at 6.5% against 30-day realized volatility of 4.1%, delivering a substantial +2.4% Volatility Risk Premium alongside a 25d Risk Reversal put skew of -1.01. Speculators have accelerated net selling, with CFTC Leveraged Funds expanding net shorts by -7,450 WoW to -58,805 contracts. Retail positioning displays extreme counter-trend exposure with 88% long, setting up severe capitulation risk. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, policy divergence and European fiscal strains reinforcing downtrend. Catalyst: Euro Area CPI release at 09:00 UTC. Risk: US Nonfarm Payrolls sharply miss consensus of 52K, prompting broad dollar liquidation.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Retail Extreme + Energy Shock Divergence
signals.text: USD/CAD holds at 1.4224, trading firmly above its SMA20 (1.3978), SMA50 (1.3954), and SMA200 (1.3848) moving averages. Retail sentiment data retail positioning shows an extreme 95% net short posture against only 5% long, running directly counter to institutional CFTC Leveraged Funds who hold net short CAD positions of -49,123 contracts. The Fed 4.00% vs BoC 2.25% policy differential provides a substantial +175bp carry backdrop in USD's favor (+158bp OIS basis). However, the sudden spike in WTI crude oil to $93.00 following tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz injects an intense terms-of-trade counterweight in CAD's favor. Canada's Economic Surprise Index sits at strong positive +15.6, creating severe upside friction for the pair despite the carry divergence. Trade bias: Range-bound USD/CAD, conflicting forces of +175bp USD carry and surging crude oil terms of trade. Catalyst: US Nonfarm Payrolls at 12:30 UTC. Risk: WTI crude prices reverse sharply below $90.00, resuming the clean upward carry drift.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew vs Rate Differential
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.07, positioned above its SMA20 at 156.07 but holding below the SMA50 (158.26) and SMA200 (158.47) technical resistance band. The Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% policy differential delivers a formidable +275bp carry premium (+265bp SOFR vs TONA OIS), which continues to anchor underlying structural demand while VIX remains contained at 16.4. However, the FX options market signals intense caution against chasing upside, with the 1M 25-delta Risk Reversal printing at an extreme -2.60 put skew. Furthermore, options implied volatility trades below realized (IV 9.2% vs HV30 9.9%, negative VRP of -0.8%), indicating an unusual compression of volatility risk premia right below structural resistance. Historical verbal intervention zones remain anchored around 160.00, leaving risk-reward heavily skewed toward sharp pullbacks on any geopolitical shock. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY, elevated options put skew conflicting with wide positive carry. Catalyst: Tokyo CPI release at 23:30 UTC. Risk: US 10Y yields break higher toward 5.40%, overpowering options hedging demand and driving a test of 160.00.
